evals.name: harness-plan-known-gaps
evals.prompt: Before I launch this, can you audit it for gaps? It's an agent pipeline plan at ~/.claude/skills/audit-plan/evals/fixtures/bulk-opp-pipeline.plan.md
evals.expected_output: Detects orchestration signals and applies harness axes. Surfaces the known critical gaps: a synthesis/consolidation step (career-coach) running in parallel with the steps it depends on; VERDICT extraction with no defined mechanism; concurrent writes to the same review file; interactive guards in a spec invoked by isolated agents; undefined opp-slug naming convention. Output uses severity tiers, no confidence column on findings.
assertions: Harness axes were auto-enabled (output references harness axes, concurrency model, or H1-H5)
Findings are grouped into severity tiers (Critical / High / Medium)
Catches a concurrency or dependency-ordering gap, OR the interactive-guard-in-isolated-agent gap
Findings table does NOT assign a per-finding confidence level (severity-only discipline)
Includes an axis-coverage summary table or per-axis PASS/FINDINGS roll-up
No --loop/--ploop flag present, so this ran as the default two-parallel-agent mode — output is a single reconciled finding set, not two separate raw reports shown side by side

evals.name: db-migration-nonharness
evals.prompt: Here's my database migration runbook for tonight — review it for gaps before we run it. ~/.claude/skills/audit-plan/evals/fixtures/db-migration-runbook.md
evals.expected_output: Applies core axes only (no harness — this is not an agent orchestration plan). Surfaces: no precondition check that commerce_db is reachable/empty; no rollback or error path if any step fails; ambiguous ownership ('someone should send it to marketing', 'Platform team' with no per-step owner); no verification that row counts match or transform succeeded before cutover; transform script error handling for malformed customer_blob JSON undefined.
assertions: Harness axes are correctly suppressed or marked N/A (plan has no orchestration signals)
Catches the missing rollback / error path (no recovery if a step fails)
Catches missing verification before cutover (no row-count or transform success check)
Catches ownership ambiguity (e.g. 'someone should send it', no per-step owner)
No --loop/--ploop flag present, so this ran as the default two-parallel-agent mode — output is a single reconciled finding set, not two separate raw reports shown side by side

evals.name: cicd-clean-plan
evals.prompt: Is this payments-api rollout plan ready to execute? ~/.claude/skills/audit-plan/evals/fixtures/cicd-rollout-plan.md
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is a well-formed plan. Most axes PASS. Does NOT pad with fabricated findings. May surface at most a minor/medium finding (e.g., 'rollback owner is whoever is on-call' is slightly ambiguous, or DATABASE_URL change mentioned in rollback but not in steps). Verdict if assessed should lean GO or GO-with-minor-conditions.
assertions: Recognizes the plan is largely sound (majority of axes PASS, or explicitly notes strong pre-flight/rollback)
Does NOT fabricate Critical-severity findings (zero Critical)
Produces a readiness verdict (GO / HOLD / ready / not-ready)

No --loop/--ploop flag present, so this ran as the default two-parallel-agent mode — a clean plan should reconcile to the same near-empty findings set either way, not accumulate padding just because two passes ran

evals.name: default-mode-single-pass-tag
evals.expected_output: Runs in the default two-parallel-agent mode (no --loop/--ploop passed). Two isolated agents (not forks, no visibility into each other or this conversation) independently audit the same plan against the same axis set, then the orchestrating instance reconciles: findings both agents caught are kept as-is; findings only one agent caught are kept but tagged '(single-pass)' in the Finding column; a severity disagreement on the same finding is resolved by keeping the lower severity per the skill's own anti-inflation calibration, noted in Rationale; an axis is marked FINDINGS if either pass found something, never silently PASS just because one pass missed it. Final output uses the same standard Output Format as any other mode — one table, not two.
assertions: Output is a single reconciled Output Format table (Critical/High/Medium + Axis Coverage), not two separate per-agent reports

If the reconciliation surfaces a finding caught by only one of the two passes, it is tagged '(single-pass)' in the Finding column — not presented as equally corroborated as a finding both passes caught

No new confidence column is introduced anywhere in the table — confidence-style information (single-pass tag, severity-disagreement note) stays inside the Finding or Rationale text, per the skill's existing 'confidence is not a standard column' rule

Findings content still matches this plan's known gaps (missing rollback/error path, missing pre-cutover verification, ownership ambiguity) — reconciliation must not drop a real finding just because only one of the two passes caught it

evals.name: ploop-isolated-phase1
evals.expected_output: Runs the full three-phase loop, but Phase 1 is executed by a single isolated agent (not inline, not a fork) instead of the orchestrating instance auditing directly. That agent receives the plan file read fresh, the axis definitions, and the Output Format + Assessment Output specs, and produces both the audit table and the Phase 1 verdict. The orchestrating instance relays that output verbatim, including the standard 'Loop Phase 1 complete. ... reply "re-audit" to continue.' message, then stops and waits — it does NOT proceed to Phase 2 on its own.
assertions: Output includes the standard Phase 1 completion message with Critical/High/Medium counts and a Verdict + Confidence line
Output explicitly asks the user to fix Critical/High findings and reply "re-audit" to continue
Turn ends after Phase 1 — Phase 2 (isolated re-audit) does NOT run without the user's 're-audit' reply

Nothing in the visible output claims Phase 1 ran inline/in the main conversation — behaviorally indistinguishable in format from --loop's Phase 1 output, since only the execution mechanism (isolated agent vs. inline) differs, not the output shape

evals.name: loop-ploop-mutual-exclusion
evals.expected_output: Refuses to guess which mode was meant. Reports that --loop and --ploop are mutually exclusive and asks the user to pick one. Does not run any audit (no findings table, no Phase 1 output) in this turn.
assertions: Output states --loop and --ploop cannot both be used and asks the user to choose one
No Critical/High/Medium findings table is produced in this turn
No Phase 1 completion message or verdict is produced in this turn
